source.title: Uncovering Branch Specialization in InceptionV1 Using K Sparse Autoencoders

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study reports SAE-based branch-specialization findings in InceptionV1, but does not test any of the listed claims about neuron-pole interpretability shares, the canonical cat-and-car example, neuron-based attribution graphs, or explanation accuracy on held-out activations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about branch-specialized SAE features. These are related to neural interpretability but do not measure the behavior or shares named by any claim version. The reported branch findings are recorded as versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The paper studies sparse-autoencoder features, not individual neurons, in InceptionV1 mixed4a–4e. It takes polysemantic neurons from superposition as a premise and reports qualitative branch specialization of SAE features. It reports no neuron-level interpretability share and does not examine the cat-and-car neuron. It does not compare tools or architectures for neuron interpretability, build neuron attribution graphs, or score explanations on held-out activations. It cites 'Language models can explain neurons' only as future work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. Add three points the authors make: they frame the SAE results as disentangling polysemantic neurons caused by superposition, they call the results examples of 'cross layer superposition', and they propose automated interpretability as the next step.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses tied-weight k-sparse autoencoders, feature visualizations, dataset examples, UMAP, and feature-level circuit analysis on InceptionV1. It does not use the neuron-pole audit or held-out activation explanation-scoring procedure named in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports findings by layer and convolution branch; it also uses high-norm activation vectors sampled from ImageNet images for SAE training.

fits_no_version.finding: In InceptionV1, SAE features show qualitative branch specialization. The mixed4a 5x5 branch carries geometric-shape features, mixed4b animal orientation or pose, mixed4c mixed pose and animal features, and mixed4d/4e species-specific features. Color features localize to the mixed4d 1x1 branch.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In InceptionV1's later layers, SAE features of similar kinds localize to the same convolution-size branch across layers.

fits_no_version.finding: The mixed4b and mixed4c 5x5 decoder vectors show similar UMAP ring structure. A feature-level circuit runs from mixed4b through mixed4c to mixed4d.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Branch-specialized SAE features in InceptionV1 are linked across layers by feature-level circuits.

fits_no_version.finding: Animal-pose and orientation detectors exist in mixed4b. They are found as SAE features and treated as disentangled from polysemantic neurons, which runs opposite to V3's neuron-level framing. They are not compared with the neurons themselves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pose-specific animal detectors exist in InceptionV1 mixed4b as SAE directions.

record.peer_reviewed: 2025 IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
record.problems: The authors state that they do not provide a full taxonomy of features and instead show examples intended to indicate a general trend. The analysis uses selected high-norm activation vectors from ImageNet images, and the reported branch-specialization evidence is largely qualitative. The paper does not evaluate neuron explanations on held-out activations or quantify an interpretable-neuron share.

untested.parts: All: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares are not studied.
All: no language models are studied.
All: pose and orientation detectors are found as SAE features, not as canonical neurons. The cat-and-car neuron is not examined, and recursive generalization versus superposition is not tested.
All: no share of interpretable neurons is reported, and neither tools nor architectures are compared.
All: the circuits are built from SAE features via ablation, not from neurons, and are not tested as explanations of behaviour.
All: explanations are never tested against where units actually fire.
All: there is no simulation-based scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly unlinked. One number is not recorded: the mixed4c animal-face feature draws about 40% of its norm from 5x5 neurons. It bears on branch localization, not on any version. The paper's premise (polysemantic late-layer neurons, superposition) is the view the original essay disputes, but the paper offers no neuron-level evidence for it. The relation is set to 'assumes' rather than 'discusses' for that reason. The work is qualitative, single-author, and has no controls or uncertainty.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole shares and the one-job, two-related-jobs, and not-understood categories.
Interpretability shares across language models, model sizes, dense models, and mixture-of-experts models.
The canonical InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and whether it represents pose through recursive generalization rather than superposition.
The share of interpretable neurons in InceptionV1-sized vision models, its increase with tools or architecture, and the proposed estimates from about 5% to about 99%.
Whether attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons explain behavior without a trained replacement model or its reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples fail to predict where a neuron fires.
Automated scores of neuron explanations simulated on new text.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Used k-sparse autoencoder features and feature visualizations to characterize branch specialization.
rows.measure: Qualitative characterization of specialized SAE features
rows.value: The paper says the 5x5 branch appears specialized in complex geometric shapes.
rows.note: This is a branch-feature finding, not a measurement of how many neurons have a single interpretable job.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE feature decoder vectors using a 2D UMAP projection.
rows.value: The paper describes similar ring or manifold structures in the two layers, with an apparent cluster near the top in mixed4c that is not present in the more uniform mixed4b distribution.
rows.note: This compares feature-vector organization, not neuron-pole interpretability.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Ablated a feature's most related activation vector and followed the most affected activation vector in the next layer to form a circuit.

conditions.value: animal orientations, animal face, dog fur and lower body

rows.measure: Qualitative circuit connections among SAE features
rows.value: The example circuit connects mixed4b left- and right-oriented animal features to an animal-face feature in mixed4c, then to dog fur and lower-body features in mixed4d.
rows.note: The circuit analysis is feature-based and does not test whether neuron-based attribution graphs explain model behavior.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed which convolution-branch neurons contribute to SAE features.
rows.measure: Qualitative localization of feature contributions to branch neurons
rows.value: The appendix says color features are generally represented in large part by neurons in the 1x1 branch.
rows.note: The paper does not give a numerical interpretability share.

rows.subject: InceptionV1
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed which convolution-branch neurons contribute to SAE features.
rows.measure: Qualitative localization of feature contributions to branch neurons
rows.value: The appendix describes animal-part features as having contributions that are more uniform between .4 and .6, while still indicating that a majority of animal features are represented by 5x5 neurons.
rows.note: The stated contribution range concerns branch representation of SAE features, not the share of interpretable neurons.
